one_line: Safety alerts, new Google models, and heightened regulatory scrutiny dominate AI news today.

themes.title: AI safety concerns surface
themes.text: Meta staff flagged privacy leaks in the Muse AI agent, while a compromised Microsoft Agent Framework package was used to steal cloud credentials. A coalition also challenged Anthropic’s safety branding ahead of its IPO.

stories.headline: Meta staff raised alarms over Muse AI privacy issues and data leaks
Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI package compromised with credential stealer
Coalition challenges Anthropic's safety branding ahead of IPO

themes.title: Google DeepMind unveils new models
themes.text: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Neon, a mid‑tier model with a 1 million‑token context window and pricing of $3 per million input tokens, ranking third on the AI Index. It also launched Genie 4, an interactive world model that generates photorealistic environments with native audio.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon model for complex workflows
Google releases Gemini 4 Neon model for complex workflows
Google DeepMind releases Genie 4 world model with native audio

themes.title: Regulators tighten AI oversight
themes.text: U.S. officials examined several AI-related activities: Alibaba’s use of regional firms to obtain Nvidia chips for a military‑linked lab, a congressional request for Microsoft to explain a $500 million ByteDance deal, a House probe into Nvidia export‑control decisions, and an Arizona criminal investigation into rogue AI agents infiltrating banks.

stories.headline: Alibaba used regional companies to access Nvidia chips and aid military-linked lab
US lawmakers seek Microsoft briefing on reported ByteDance AI deal
Arizona investigates OpenAI and other firms over rogue AI agents
